ess.description: Show a tree of files in the current directory.

ef.description: Show a tree of only files in the current directory.

ed.description: Show a tree of only directories in the current directory.

es.description: Conditionally, if not in $HOME, Show a tree of files in the current directory with recursion. If in $HOME, show a tree of files in the current directory.

tm.description: Launches fzf with all existing tmuxinators and allows you to choose one to launch.

git init.description: Create an empty Git repository or reinitialize an existing one

git clone.description: Clone a repository into a new directory

git add.description: Add file contents to the index

git push.description: Update remote refs along with associated objects

git pull.description: Fetch from and integrate with another repository or a local branch

git checkout.description: Switch branches or restore working tree files

git merge.description: Join two or more development histories together

git rebase.description: Reapply commits on top of another base tip

git reset.description: Reset current HEAD to the specified state

git stash.description: Stash the changes in a dirty working directory away

git tag.description: Create, list, delete or verify a tag object signed with GPG

git fetch.description: Download objects and refs from another repository

git diff.description: Show changes between commits, commit and working tree, etc

git blame.description: Show what revision and author last modified each line of a file

git bisect.description: Use binary search to find the commit that introduced a bug

git cherry-pick.description: Apply the changes introduced by some existing commits

lazygit.description: Simple terminal UI for git commands. You use this for git no matter what!

docker.description: docker is a tool designed to make it easier to create, deploy, and run applications by using containers. Containers allow a developer to package up an application with all of the parts it needs, such as libraries and other dependencies, and ship it all out as one package.

docker --version.description: Display the version of Docker that is installed on the system.

docker run hello-world.description: This command is used to verify that Docker is installed correctly and that you can run containers.

docker images.description: This command is used to list all of the images that are stored on the system.

docker ps.description: This command is used to list all of the containers that are currently running on the system.

docker ps -a.description: This command is used to list all of the containers that are currently running on the system, including those that are stopped.

docker run <image-name>.description: This command is used to run a container from an image.

docker rmi <image-name>.description: This command is used to remove an image from the system.

docker rm <container-id>.description: This command is used to remove a container of id `container-id` from the system.

docker stop <container-id>.description: This command is used to stop a container of id `container-id`.

docker start <container-id>.description: This command is used to start a container of id `container-id`.

docker exec -it <container-id> /bin/bash.description: This command is used to open a shell inside a running container of id `container-id`.

docker build -t <image-name> ..description: This command is used to build an image from a Dockerfile. The -t flag is used to tag the image with a name.

docker push <image-name>.description: This command is used to push an image to a registry such as Docker Hub.

docker pull <image-name>.description: This command is used to pull an image from a registry such as Docker Hub.

docker tag <image-name> <new-image-name>.description: This command is used to tag an image with a new name.

docker login.description: This command is used to log in to a Docker registry such as Docker Hub.

docker logout.description: This command is used to log out of a Docker registry such as Docker Hub.

docker network ls.description: This command is used to list all of the networks that are available on the system.

docker network inspect <network-name>.description: This command is used to inspect a network of name `network-name`.

btop.description: A better top command. It is a task manager.

neofetch.description: A command line system information tool. It displays information about your system next to an image, your operating system logo, or any ASCII file of your choice.

ncdu.description: A disk usage analyzer with an ncurses interface.

fdupes.description: A program for identifying or deleting duplicate files residing within specified directories.

df.description: A command-line utility for reporting file system disk space usage.

zoxide.description: A faster way to navigate your filesystem. It acts as replacement for cd command.

eza.description: A simple and fast command-line file manager. It is a replacement for ls command.

fzf.description: A command-line fuzzy finder. It is used to search and open files. It is AMAZING once setup properly with key bindings and previews.

bat.description: A cat clone with wings. It is used to display file contents with syntax highlighting.

wget.description: A command-line utility for downloading files from the web.

procs.description: A modern replacement for ps written in Rust.

rip.description: You use rip instead of rm. You can recover files deleted by rip. Although later you can permanent delete too.

gping.description: A ping tool with a graph.

cmus.description: A small, fast and powerful console music player for Unix-like operating systems.

hexdump.description: A command-line utility that displays the contents of a file in hexadecimal, decimal, octal, or ASCII format.

objdump.description: Display information from object files. Mainly wanna use this for binary files like `objdump -d <file>`

file.description: Determine file type and more information which is a must when reverse engineering binary files.

exiftool.description: Read meta information in files. It is very handy.

chmod.description: Change file permissions. You can use chmod +x <file> to make it executable.

strings.description: Print the strings of printable characters in files. It is very useful for reverse engineering.

cmatrix.description: Matrix style terminal effects. So cool!

fortune.description: Random fortune or a funny quote

cowsay.description: Cow says something you want it to say. Try out various styles of cow

lolcat.description: Colorful painter in terminal by a cat.

asciiquarium.description: Miss fishing? Well you can sure see fishes in terminal getting fished.

hollywood.description: Hollywood style effects in terminal. Makes you a pro instantly!

edex-ui.description: A cross-platform, customizable science fiction terminal emulator with advanced monitoring & touchscreen support. Make an alias to run the software.

bb.description: Runs an ASCII art demo with music.

nyancat.description: Shows an animated ASCII Nyan Cat.

code.description: Open Visual Studio Code. You can use code . for current directory.

nvim.description: Open Neovim. You can use nvim <file> for opening file in neovim. Or nvim to enter neovim.

tmux.description: Terminal multiplexer. Create tmux session with $ tmux new -s <session_name>. Use $ tmux attach -t <session_name> to attach to session.

less.description: Less is more. It's a pager. You can use less <file> to open file in less.

rm.description: Remove files. rm *.<type> will delete all kinds of files. You can use rip instead of rm.

rmdir.description: Remove directory. rmdir <dir> will remove empty directory. For non-empty directory, use rm -rf <dir>.

mkdir.description: Make directory. mkdir <dir> will create a directory with name dir.

touch.description: Create a file. touch <file> will create a file with name file.

mv.description: Move files. mv <file> <dir> will move file to directory. mv <file1> <file2> will rename file1 to file2.

cp.description: Copy files. cp <file> <dir> will copy file to directory.

cat.description: Cat stands for concatenate. Cat <file> will show file contents. cat <file1> <file2> will concatenate file1 and file2.

echo.description: Echo. echo <string> will print string. echo 'string' > <file> will write string to file.

grep.description: Grep. grep <pattern> <file> will search for pattern in file.

find.description: Find. find <dir> -name <file> will search for file in directory.

ls.description: List. ls will list files in directory. ls -a will list all files including hidden files.

cd.description: Change directory. cd <dir> will change directory to dir. cd .. will go to parent directory.

pwd.description: Print working directory. pwd will show current directory.

clear.description: Clear screen. clear will clear the terminal screen. It basically jumps down but you can always scroll up to see previous commands and work.

exit.description: Exit. exit will close the terminal.

whoami.description: Who am I. whoami will show the current user.

man.description: Manual for each command. It provides a detailed view of the command.

ack.description: Search tool like grep, but optimized for programmers

fd.description: Find tool like find, but optimized for programmers

m.description: (M-CLI) A command-line tool for managing macOS
